summary: For every alpha>0 there are two independent cap-one original variables whose orthogonal product projection (S,R) has joint density cap <=1 but E||p_{S|R}||_infinity^alpha is unbounded (and is infinite for alpha>=2). For 0<alpha<2 an explicit N-fragment construction gives a lower bound [2^(1-alpha/2)/(2-alpha)](N-1)N^(alpha-1) ~ N^alpha. At alpha=2/3 the cost grows ~N^(2/3). The same source embeds in a target-valid Q=S^2+Y^2-Z^2 with eigenvalues {1,1,-1,0} and ||p_Q||_infinity<=pi/sqrt(2). Thus conditioning the residual product-projection coordinate and averaging any positive power of its conditional density cap is not a valid dimension-free proof interface; aggregation must remain unconditional.
